In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: {\em (i)} What is the optimal decay rate of solutions to a system of evolution equations, when the damping is only present in a part of the system, and the damping is {\em not} directly coupled to the other parts of the system? {\em (ii)} How can one obtain a full range of optimal decay rates, and what are the optimal estimates with respect to initial data, when damping is present only in a part of a system? {\em iii)}
the following questions: {\em What are the minimal assumptions for the damping terms, in order to guarantee polynomial decay of the solutions?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to treat the stabilization of weakly damped systems, with hybrid boundary conditions, by means of indirect stabilization.
we are able to stabilize a system of two hyperbolic equations with a single damping acting on the second equation, and with no boundary damping at all.
we provide new results for indirect damping, with a focus on the coupling of two different systems with different damping mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of hybrid boundary conditions, the stability properties of the system are determined by the {\em slow} component.
, under suitable compatibility assumptions, the energy of the coupled system decays at a rate that is not worse than the fastest decay rate of each individual component.
the coupling of the two systems can lead to a significant increase of the rate of decay of the energy.
